deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 118r holds drafts of private letters, written in pencil with many deletions. They date from late November 1863, when Riemann was living in Pisa. The next page carries the dated French fair draft: 'Pise, 29 Novembre 1863, B. Riemann, professeur, Via del Museo, Casa Papini[?], 1° piano'.

(a) Top of the page: trial salutations for a German letter. The address is 'Sr. Hochwürden dem Herrn Pastor Dr. Détroit', with the salutations 'Hochgeehrter Herr Pastor' and 'Verehrteste Frau Pastorin'. This is evidently the German Protestant pastor (and his wife), probably in Livorno.

(b) The main German draft explains the situation. The Riemanns had long been expecting a crate sent on the forwarding route via Marseille. It contained winter clothing for Riemann's wife and another family member, and things for 'das hier erwartete Kleine', the child expected in Pisa. Riemann's daughter Ida was born in Pisa in December 1863. Riemann is now in the greatest embarrassment and anxiety. A letter from Herr Romagne[?] in Marseille says the crate was shipped to Livorno on 18 November by a steamer of the Compagnie Valéry, so it must already have been in Livorno for about fourteen days. When Riemann was in Livorno on 16 November, he had already asked about the crate at the Valéry office. He was promised that it would be forwarded to him immediately on arrival.

(c) Bottom of the page: a French draft to 'Monsieur Angelo Alhaique', with the trial salutation 'Signor stimatissimo'. Riemann announces that he intends to come to Livorno to present the letter of credit from Messrs Baur of Altona that is in his possession.

The following page continues the same matter. It is a French letter to Messieurs Valéry in Livorno, giving the crate as 'R. 3. – 1 caisse vieux livres K: 215' and asking that it be sent by rail to Pisa.

The page serves no mathematical problem. It is biographical material from Riemann's stay in Italy, where he went for his health.

results.what: Draft letters, non-mathematical, about a delayed crate of winter effects shipped Marseille to Livorno (Compagnie Valéry), plus a draft about presenting a Baur (Altona) letter of credit to Angelo Alhaique in Livorno, November 1863

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics, only household correspondence drafts from Riemann's 1863 stay in Pisa. It is of minor biographical interest: it confirms the dates, the Livorno and Marseille shipping arrangements, his Pisa address, and the family awaiting a child (Ida, born December 1863).
transcription_corrections: 'Die erwarteten seit längerer Zeit' is more likely 'Wir erwarteten seit längerer Zeit eine Kiste ...'.

'auf die Winter gesandeln [?] für meine Frau' probably refers to winter clothing ('...Winterkleider[?] für meine Frau ...'). The French version on the next page says 'effets ... nécessaires pour l'hiver, à moi et à ma famille'.
'Besitzung [?] für das hier erwartete [?] ...' most plausibly reads '... für das hier erwartete Kleine enthielt', meaning things for the expected baby (Ida Riemann, born Pisa, December 1863).
The second family member after 'Frau und' may be 'Schwester' or 'Schwägerin'. The word is uncertain in the image.
'Ich bin [?] ... höchst [?] mit der größten Verlegenheit' is probably 'Ich bin daher jetzt in der größten Verlegenheit und Beunruhigung ...'. The reading is uncertain.
The Marseille agent's name is spelled 'Romagne' here and 'Romagnier[?]' on the next page. The same person is meant, and the correct spelling is uncertain.
'Verehrtester Frau Pastorin' should read 'Verehrteste Frau Pastorin'.
